method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the writing-l4-rules skill; the three duties the Law states in days (s 149(1) 60 days, s 192(2)(b) 30 days, s 130(1) 7 days) are regulative rules (PARTY ... MUST ... WITHIN ... HENCE FULFILLED LEST BREACH ... BECAUSE) and the seat questions read plain dates; no REFUSE (gaps answer `not covered`, asserted); every judgment of a Board, panel or court asked as an input; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (Western Australia), compilation on the Western Australian Legislation website (mrdoc_49311), retrieved 2026-09-07, including the Queensland amendments of 2022 (Act 22 of 2022) and 2025 (Act 6 of 2025) commenced in WA (last listed commencement 10 April 2026; ss 237A, 237B from 1 December 2025), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_49311.txt; with the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law Application Act 2024 (WA) (mrdoc_49650, retrieved 2026-09-07) for ss 19, 27, 28. The Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (WA) Act 2010 named in the work list was repealed by the 2024 Act s 38. Registration standards and national regulations not deposited; none sets a number used.

checks.command: l4 run hpnl-dates.l4 ; l4 run hpnl-notifier.l4 ; l4 run hpnl-cases-notifier.l4
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. A breached DEONTIC cannot be compared with EQUALS on this l4, so the three regulative rules are asserted through CONSIDER EVALTRACE ... WHEN FULFILLED.

scope: s 5 (definitions used); s 129; s 130(1), (2), (3)(c); ss 138, 139A, 139B; Part 8 Div 2 (ss 140-143, with WA s 141(4)(ca) and the deletions of s 141(2A), ss 141A-141C by the Application Act 2024 ss 27, 28); Div 3 (ss 144, 145); Div 4 (ss 146, 147); s 149(1); s 150(1)-(4); s 151; s 152; ss 159A, 161(3)(b), (4), 167A, 177A, 180(1)(b), (2), 187, 189, 192(2)(b), (4); ss 237, 237A, 237B; Sch 7 cl 31(2), (3) (weekends only). Out: Parts 1-7 otherwise (machinery, registration, title and practice protections ss 113-123A, advertising); Part 8 procedure and powers otherwise (Divs 5-14, including interim prohibition orders and public statements); Parts 9-12 otherwise; the rest of the Application Act 2024.
seat: the notifier: usually a patient, or a patient's family member, harmed by or worried about a registered health practitioner's care or conduct, who may also be bringing or settling a negligence claim
